parent: Careforsons Ltd (trading as Sons), company number 11557956, London. Sister sites sons.ie and sonshaar.de.
model: Men-only UK hair-loss subscription brand. Its own Shopify store and consultation app sell licensed finasteride 1 mg and minoxidil 5% (Sons holds the licences), unlicensed compounded sprays and capsules, supplements and shampoos; prescribing and dispensing are done by a partner, The Independent Pharmacy (ABSM Healthcare Ltd, GPhC 9012559).

access.accountWall: After the last consent screen (finasteride statement). The next screen is an account form (first name, last name, email, phone, date of birth, password) titled "Based on your questionnaire results, we are now preparing your personalised health plan. Please complete your account set up to continue." No recommendation, product or price is shown before it. Pressing "Get my personalised plan" creates the account and sends the consultation together. Answering "Yes" to "Are you an existing Sons customer?" hits the sign-in page at question 1.
blockers: sons.co.uk/agents.md (listed in the sitemap) returned a Cloudflare "Verifying your connection" check to curl; not pursued.
Recommendation, plan choice, basket and checkout screens need an account, so they were read from served code only.
access.coverageNote: Walked live with the baseline man to the account form (11 screens), then once more with every branch switched on, so all 24 conditional screens were also seen live. The baseline woman is stopped at question 2. The full question set (38 pages) was read from the survey definition the page itself downloads, and the rules that turn answers into plans were read from two copies of the recommendation code that the site serves to anonymous visitors. Nothing behind the account form was tested live: no account, email, phone or order was created. Product strengths come from public leaflets and the shop app code; prices from the public product feed.

flows.name: Hair-loss consultation (the only route in for scalp hair loss; survey code uk_consultation)
flows.stagesSummary: 2 gate questions (existing customer, sex at birth) → self-declaration tick → 6 core screens for a healthy man (picture, onset, mood, past medicines, format preference, conditions) with up to 24 extra conditional screens → finasteride statement and optional NHS/GP consents → ACCOUNT WALL (account form; consultation is sent with it) → recommendation page, plan length, basket, checkout, identity check, prescriber review (not tested; read from code and public pages).

entryPoints.label: "Start consultation" on sons.co.uk/pages/consultation-hair (linked from the home page, menu "Consultation", and the "Get started" button on almost every hair product and plan page)

URL switches read by the app, all loading the same questions: combo_pill=true, from_clinic=yes, from_ksl_clinic=yes, bhc-clinic=yes (send the man to a "combo" recommendation page), is_google=true (recommendation/google), health_check=true (repeat health check for subscribers), clinic_consultation + clinic_id (partner clinic), customer=<token> (auto sign-in)
Product pages for Oral Minoxidil 5mg, Combination Capsule, Dutasteride spray, Topical Finasteride and Topical Finasteride & Oral Minoxidil show "Log In" instead of "Get started"
No consultation at all: Non-Prescription plan, Hair Growth Complex, biotin, shampoo, conditioner, clay, dermaroller have plan pickers / "Add to cart" on their pages

questions.text: Please select the image that best describes your hair loss:

options.label: Temples only (receding at the front)
options.effect: No effect on the plans shown: the answer is stored and sent with the consultation, but neither copy of the served recommendation code reads it. What the server or the prescriber does with it is unknown. Typical male pattern.

options.label: Temples/Crown
options.effect: No effect on the plans shown: the answer is stored and sent with the consultation, but neither copy of the served recommendation code reads it. What the server or the prescriber does with it is unknown. Typical male pattern (used for the baseline man).

options.label: Random patches
options.effect: No effect on the plans shown: the answer is stored and sent with the consultation, but neither copy of the served recommendation code reads it. What the server or the prescriber does with it is unknown. Patchy loss would normally point away from male pattern baldness, yet no warning or stop appears. Whether the prescriber acts on it is unknown.

options.label: Completely bald
options.effect: No effect on the plans shown: the answer is stored and sent with the consultation, but neither copy of the served recommendation code reads it. What the server or the prescriber does with it is unknown. No stop screen appears even though treatment cannot help a fully bald scalp. The app code knows notice pages called "extensive-loss-notice" and "Sudden Hair Loss Notice" (from another market or an earlier version), but the current UK questionnaire contains neither.

questions.text: Please confirm that you've read and understood the following:
questions.detail: Please confirm that you've read and understood the following: It's important to be aware that if you experience any side effects, please stop taking the treatments and speak to your doctor as soon as possible. Finasteride can very rarely cause changes in mood, including depression, or changes in sexual function. These effects usually resolve after stopping treatment, and your doctor can explore other options to support your hair loss goals. Read more You must stop using Finasteride-containing products at least 3 months prior to trying for a baby/conception, and must not continue with using Finasteride-containing products unless at least 3-months post-conception. Further information can be found here: https://mothertobaby.org/fact-sheets/finasteride/ Sons are license holders and hold Marketing Authorisation for Finasteride 1mg and 5% Minoxidil solution. Other treatment plans can contain different preparations of medications such as Minoxidil and Finasteride which are off-license usage or unlicensed 'specials' which are produced by a specials manufacturer.

recommendations.profile: Man, 32, temples and crown, gradual onset, no mood concerns, no past treatment, no conditions, "I don't mind" on format (the baseline man)
recommendations.note: READ FROM CODE, NOT SEEN LIVE (the page needs an account). Older page script on sons.co.uk/pages/recommendation: two primary cards, Core Plan (opening on the capsule version, spray on a toggle) and the Combination Spray; the other ten sit under "See more plans". Newer app code at shop.sons.co.uk/recommendation: one primary card, the Combination Spray, then the rest. Which copy a new customer lands on today was not confirmed; the consultation code redirects to the sons.co.uk page. The newer function was also run offline on these answers (node scripts/engine-run.js) and returned the Combination Spray as the primary card.
Stopped at question 2 with a notice to see a GP or hair-loss specialist. The medical FAQ adds that 5% minoxidil "cannot be sold to females as Sons are not permitted to do so under UK licensing".

engineSummary: One short questionnaire for men only. It never stops a man before the account form: sex at birth is the only gate. Every clinical answer is carried forward and, after sign-up, a script running in the customer's browser turns the answers into five on/off switches (finasteride tablet, finasteride spray, minoxidil capsule, minoxidil spray, combination spray). Each ticked condition or reported side effect flips whole drug families off, a fixed ordered list of twelve plans is filtered by those switches, and the format preference only picks which of two orders is used. The top one or two survivors are shown as the recommendation. The partner pharmacy's prescriber reviews the order afterwards. Rules below are read from the served code, not yet replayed.
strengths: Very short: a healthy man clicks through 10 screens before the account form, most of them one tap.
Holds its own UK licences for finasteride 1 mg and minoxidil 5%, and says so; it is open that sprays and capsules are unlicensed specials.
Wide format choice (tablet, spray, capsule, combined spray, combined capsule) with a Spray/Capsule toggle on each plan card.
PHQ-2 style mood questions and a finasteride safety statement sit inside the flow.
Optional NHS Summary Care Record and GP-sharing consents.
Money-back "Sons Promise" after six months, a repeat health check before renewals, and a partner-clinic programme for transplant patients.
weaknesses: No recommendation, price or product is shown until the visitor hands over name, email, phone, date of birth and a password.

The hair picture (including "Random patches" and "Completely bald") and the sudden-onset follow-ups do not change what is offered in the served code; a man with sudden patchy loss is still shown minoxidil and a supplement.
Age is not asked before the wall; the over-65 rule differs between the two code copies and from the product pages (18-75 for finasteride).
No questions on current medicines (apart from one yes/no after sudden onset), allergies, low blood pressure, family history, how long hair has been thinning, or goals.
The whole rule set runs in the browser and is readable by anyone, with a hidden "Debug (Dev Only)" block of reasons in the page.
Women are turned away with no alternative product or signposting beyond "see a GP".

Small wording and data slips: "Is their hair loss over other parts of your body?", the drawing for "Random patches" looks like a larger temples-and-crown pattern rather than patches, product pages that disagree with the leaflet on the combination spray strength.
opportunities: Show a provisional plan and price before asking for contact details.
Use the pattern picture and onset answers for real triage (stop or refer for patchy, sudden or scarring loss) and explain why.
Serve women, whom Sons refuses outright.
Ask about current medicines, blood pressure and goals, and explain each exclusion to the patient instead of silently hiding plans.
Offer a clear route for men over 65 and men trying for a baby.

limitations: Nothing after the account form was seen live. The recommendation rules are read from code the site serves; the server may add or override them (it can send its own ordered list and sets account tags such as finasteride_disallowed).
What the prescriber at the partner pharmacy does with the answers, how often orders are refused, and whether photos are ever requested are unknown.
Two copies of the recommendation code disagree in places (order of the list, number of primary cards, over-65 rule). Which one new customers see was not confirmed.
Prices are list prices on one day during a Black Friday sale; first-order discounts change often.
Legal class of the minoxidil spray and ketoconazole shampoo (P or GSL) was not checked against the MHRA register.
The exact wording of checkout consents (pharmacy disclaimer, ketoconazole terms) is not served to anonymous visitors.
